summary: The first memo in the new FYI (For Your Information) sub-series of RFCs. It introduces the series and specifies no standard. It is historic and was replaced by RFC 6360.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1150 introduces FYI notes, an informational subseries of RFCs about Internet topics. It describes their purpose, format, relationship to other FYIs, and how readers could obtain them; RFC 6360 later obsoleted this memo.

questions: what is the difference between rfc and fyi
where do i find fyi notes
what is the purpose of the fyi series
subtitle: An introduction to FYI notes as an informational subseries of RFCs.

tldr.problem: Readers need informational material about Internet topics in addition to protocol specifications.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1150 introduces FYIs as an RFC subseries for information ranging from historical explanations to operational answers.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1150 was obsoleted by RFC 6360 and does not specify a standard.

today: RFC 1150 is Historic and was obsoleted by RFC 6360.

sections.title: What FYI Notes Are For
sections.content:
FYI means For Your Information. The series is intended as a central repository of information about Internet topics. Topics may include why something was done a particular way or answers to commonly asked operational questions.

The intended audience ranges from beginners to people interested in advanced topics. The RFC says anyone with something to contribute may submit an FYI.
sections.plainLanguage: FYIs share information about Internet topics rather than define a protocol standard. They can be written for readers with different levels of experience.

sections.title: Why FYIs Are Part of the RFC Series
sections.content: The RFC gives several reasons for keeping FYIs in the RFC series. Its distribution mechanisms were already established, the RFC maintenance mechanisms were already in place and funded, and the RFC name carried credibility in the Internet community.
sections.plainLanguage: FYIs use the existing RFC distribution and maintenance system. Readers who know how to find RFCs can also find FYIs.

sections.title: Format, References, and Distribution
sections.content:
FYIs must follow the RFC format rules referenced in RFC 1111. The memo describes the terms UPDATES and OBSOLETES: an obsoleting document replaces the earlier document and can stand on its own, while an update supplements an earlier document.

RFC 1150 also describes how FYIs were announced and obtained at the time, including FTP and an automatic mail service. It states that security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: FYIs follow RFC formatting rules. A later FYI can either replace an earlier one or add information that must be read with it.
